chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Nahr is at the throat hollow, and dhabḥ is at the throat."

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: title of Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in the chain
key_terms.الذَّبْحُ: slaughter by cutting in the prescribed place of the neck
key_terms.اللَّبَّةِ: the throat hollow or upper chest area where nahr is performed
key_terms.النَّحْرُ: the method of slaughtering by piercing in the prescribed place, especially for camels
key_terms.الْحَلْقِ: the throat or neck region where dhabḥ is performed

ai.seo_question: Where is nahr performed, and where is dhabḥ performed in Islamic slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith states the proper location for nahr and dhabḥ in ritual slaughter. It distinguishes between the method used for animals such as camels and the method used in ordinary slaughter, providing a concise fiqh ruling.
